purpose: Screen the San Agustin Table 1 labels Oreochromis niloticus and Rhinogobius sp. against the existing name crosswalk and independent Philippine freshwater literature.

method.scope: Focused current-name and Philippine freshwater-context review of the verbatim labels Oreochromis niloticus and Rhinogobius sp.
method.distinction: The GBIF crosswalk identifies O. niloticus at accepted species rank but can only match Rhinogobius sp. to the genus Rhinogobius. An independent 2018-2019 Tablas wetland inventory lists O. niloticus as introduced in site code SAg (San Agustin); that separate survey does not identify the specimens in the 2025 estuary/tributary paper. Philippine Rhinogobius literature documents multiple distinct species but supplies no San Agustin identification for the genus-only label.
method.evidenceLimit: Gonzalez et al. surveyed freshwater bodies across nine Tablas municipalities and deposited samples in the RSU-San Agustin Campus Biological Repository, but the article does not link its O. niloticus checklist row to a repository accession. Maeda et al. document Philippines-level genus context, two distinct Palawan species, and three named Luzon species, while noting that historical Negros and Leyte records are taxonomically uncertain. Neither source links a specimen to the 2025 survey's label or reach.
method.sourceReuse: Only attributed summary findings and direct citations are retained. No specimen image, sequence, coordinates, or source-table extract was copied. Research-only; no public-app publication or derived checklist is approved.

findings.nameCrosswalk: The existing strict GBIF Backbone crosswalk returned an exact accepted species-rank match (usage key 4285694; confidence 98) for Oreochromis niloticus. Retain the source spelling; this is a nomenclatural match, not specimen verification.
findings.currentAuthority: The accepted species-rank GBIF match is consistent with the printed binomial. The independent Tablas survey also prints the same name and labels it introduced; this supports regional context, not an identification of the separate 2025 survey material.
findings.philippineContext: Gonzalez, Gado, and Mantes (2023) sampled streams, rivers, creeks, irrigation water, marshes, and idle fishponds across nine Tablas municipalities during 2018-2019. Their checklist marks O. niloticus as introduced and lists site code SAg, which the article's note defines as San Agustin. The paper reports specimens were stored at the RSU-San Agustin Campus Biological Repository, but its O. niloticus entry has no linked repository accession in the published table.
findings.disposition: An independent freshwater inventory supports San Agustin-area context for the name and its introduced status. No new range-authority discrepancy or voucher-priority mismatch is added. The identity, exact site, and reach of the O. niloticus label in the 2025 estuary/tributary study remain unverified.
findings.priority: request the 2025 RSU specimen accession and sequence-to-voucher crosswalk; keep the independent 2018-2019 freshwater report as separate attributed evidence

findings.nameCrosswalk: The existing strict GBIF Backbone crosswalk matched this genus-only label at genus rank (Rhinogobius; usage key 2377576; match type HIGHERRANK; confidence 95). It did not resolve a species. Preserve the literal sp. qualifier.
findings.currentAuthority: The label is already genus-level, so no species-level accepted name can be assigned from it. Maeda et al. (2021) describe Rhinogobius estrellae and R. tandikan from separate Palawan streams, discuss three named Luzon species, and distinguish species using diagnostic morphology and phylogenetic evidence. The paper states historical Negros and Leyte material attributed to Rhinogobius is uncertain because the old Bureau of Science specimens were destroyed and early taxonomy was misconstrued.
findings.philippineContext: Published work establishes Philippine genus-level context, including streams in Palawan and named species in Luzon. The 2023 Tablas-wide freshwater checklist does not list Rhinogobius; that non-mention is not evidence of absence and does not refine the 2025 survey label. No reviewed source identifies a Rhinogobius specimen from the San Agustin survey's sites.
findings.disposition: Keep Rhinogobius sp. at genus rank. Do not infer a species from geographic plausibility, neighboring islands, or the GBIF genus match. No new range-authority discrepancy or voucher-priority mismatch is added; local identity and reach remain unresolved.
findings.priority: obtain the RSU specimen catalogue number and diagnostic images or character data before any species-level reassessment; confirm whether a sequence is directly linked to that voucher

nextAction: Screen the remaining five Table 1 labels against current fish authorities and locality-resolved Philippine sources. Keep the six voucher-priority mismatch labels and five unresolved authority/range issues in their separate queues. Then seek the RSU voucher/accession crosswalk and resolve the survey's station/locality conflicts before considering occurrence rows.

sources.supports: The 2025 San Agustin survey labels, stated repository holding, missing public specimen accession identifiers, and survey-locality limitations.
Accepted species-rank GBIF Backbone match for Oreochromis niloticus (usage key 4285694; confidence 98).
Existing crosswalk's genus-rank Rhinogobius match for the literal source label Rhinogobius sp.; no species resolution.

Gonzalez, Gado, and Mantes (2023), Tablas Island wetland survey across nine municipalities and multiple freshwater habitat types; its checklist marks O. niloticus introduced at SAg (San Agustin) and describes RSU repository storage.
Maeda et al. (2021), two distinct voucher-based Rhinogobius species described from Palawan; three named Luzon species; and uncertainty about historical Negros/Leyte reports.
